# Preface {.unnumbered}

This is a book about deciding.

Not about AI in general, though you'll learn a lot of that on the way. It's about one narrow, very common job: looking at a situation and choosing what to do. Is this email phishing? Which team gets this ticket? Is this payment safe? Should this agent call that tool?

Software makes millions of these decisions every day, and more and more of them are handed to large language models. LLMs are superb at reading and writing. But a decision isn't a paragraph. It's a choice between a few options, made without being sure, with a price for getting it wrong. To make one well you need three things:

- a **probability you can trust**, one that means what it says;
- a **threshold set by what mistakes cost**, not by habit;
- a clear rule for **when to hand the case to a person**.

Most people building with AI today have none of the three. This book gives you all of them, from first principles, in plain language.

In 2026 a company called TypeSafe AI released Jev, which it calls the first **System One model**: a model that never writes, and only answers typed questions with probabilities, in one fast pass [@typesafe2026]. You'll learn to test whether Jev does what its makers claim. But the idea behind it outlives any one product: some decisions belong in a separate, fast, measurable layer of an AI system, and that layer needs different skills from the rest.

## Three rules I followed

**No invented measurements.** I had no access to Jev's API while writing, so every Jev number comes from a stand-in that copies its public interface, and is marked *synthetic* every time. These numbers show you how to reason and test; they're not claims about the real model.

**Vendor claims are labelled.** When I report what TypeSafe says about Jev, I say it's *vendor-reported* and cite the source.

**Claims go in piles.** Everything said about Jev is sorted into what I could check, what the vendor reports, and what nobody outside the company knows yet. Chapter 9 explains how. Use the same three piles for anything you read about new models, this book included.
